themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK, a 400% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 1.0 complaint per week (z-score: 5.66), suggesting a widespread environmental health issue affecting multiple buildings in Hunts Point/Longwood.
evidence: 5 indoor air quality complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.66 indicates statistically significant spike
Concurrent spike in general Air Quality complaints (5 complaints 2 weeks ago, up 567% from 0.8 baseline)
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents: Are they experiencing mold, ventilation failures, or chemical odors? Do complaints cluster in specific buildings?
Investigate whether complaints correlate with recent construction activity (226 DOB permit filings in last 90 days, 176 alterations)
Contact HPD/DOB to determine which buildings are under investigation and whether violations are being issued

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints reached 4 THIS WEEK, a 220% spike above the 8-week average of 1.2 per week (z-score: 4.16), indicating rapid deterioration of sanitary conditions across multiple locations in the district.
evidence: 4 rodent complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.16 reflects significant statistical deviation
Unsanitary conditions already represent 500 total complaints over 90 days, suggesting underlying sanitation failures
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks: Are complaints clustered in specific neighborhoods or building types? Interview residents about visible evidence.
Cross-reference with DOH pest control inspection records to determine response times and enforcement actions
Investigate whether garbage collection frequency or street sanitation is adequate for the neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Curb Deterioration in Hunts Point
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 2300% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.1 complaints per week (z-score: 8.69, highest severity), indicating acute street infrastructure failure affecting pedestrian and vehicular safety.
evidence: 3 curb condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 is the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset
Concurrent spike in Illegal Parking (602 complaints over 90 days) and Blocked Driveway (242 complaints), suggesting curb management is strained
reporting_angles: Identify specific streets with deteriorated curbs: Walk the neighborhood and photograph conditions. Are certain areas worse?
File FOIL request for DOT work orders and maintenance schedules in CD 202 to assess frequency of curb repairs
Determine whether curb damage is linked to heavy commercial traffic, weather events, or deferred maintenance cycles

themes_detail.label: Elevator Safety & Access Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints peaked at 26 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO, a 259% increase over the 8-week baseline of 7.2 per week (z-score: 7.39), raising concerns about accessibility and building code compliance in multi-story housing stock, though the spike has since moderated.
evidence: 26 elevator complaints filed 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 7.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.39 reflects one of the most severe spikes in dataset
Community board budget requests repeatedly call for 'Assign additional building inspectors,' suggesting chronic DOB enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Interview elderly and disabled residents: How long have elevators been broken? Are they trapped on upper floors?
Cross-reference complaint addresses with DOB violation database to determine which buildings are repeat offenders and why repairs are delayed
Investigate whether the spike correlates with specific buildings under new ownership or management, or with seasonal maintenance cycles

themes_detail.label: Building Code & Use Violations
themes_detail.summary: Building/use violations spiked to 6 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO, a 700% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.8 per week (z-score: 7.94), suggesting potential illegal conversions, overcrowding, or unpermitted commercial operations, though this spike has moderated.
evidence: 6 building/use complaints filed 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.94 reflects statistically severe deviation
226 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (176 alterations, 21 new buildings) suggest active construction activity that may be driving non-compliance
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaint addresses with active DOB permits and violations to identify buildings operating outside approved scope
Interview DOB about enforcement capacity: Are inspectors responsive to complaints? What is the average violation-to-closure timeline?
Investigate whether violations relate to affordable housing pressures (overcrowding, illegal conversions) or commercial encroachment into residential areas
